steps.observation: You have 900 seconds. Write a short story about a lighthouse keeper.

steps.action:
Eamon stood at the top of the spiral staircase, wind-lashed salt spray stinging his face. Tonight’s storm was the fiercest he’d seen in twenty years as keeper of Black Rock Light. His left hand gripped the brass railing; with his right, he consulted the pocket watch ticking down from 900 seconds.

A fishing schooner’s faint distress signal crackled over his crackling radio: “Lifeline broken—approaching jagged shoals—help!” The beam of Black Rock Light had inexplicably gone dark. Without it, the ship would founder in minutes.

Eamon dashed down the stairs, every footfall echoing. He reached the lamp chamber, heart pounding. The automatic winder had jammed. There was only time to free the mechanism by hand, then refill the lamp with precious oil soaked in cedar wicks. He yanked at rusted gears, the storm’s fury rattling the old tower. Sixty seconds left.

With trembling fingers, he rekindled the flame. The glass lens blazed to life just as the schooner’s lookout shouted a last warning. Beadlike waves threatened to swallow the vessel whole—but the lighthouse beam sliced through the darkness, guiding her clear.

As the ship’s horn boomed a salute, Eamon exhaled, chest heaving. He glanced again at the watch: five seconds before midnight. The storm still raged, but hope had held fast.
